candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure gate identifier. Also called: gate number, boarding gate, flight gate. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure gate "Gate A12", "Flight UA123" departure gate "Gate 34B". Distinct from arrivalGate, which is the arrival gate.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: departureTerminal
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.

candidates.label: tripOrigin
candidates.comment: A trip origin relation between a trip and its starting location, prior to any destinations. Also called starting point, departure location, point of origin. Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".

chosen_property.label: travelledTo
chosen_property.definition: To have moved to a particular location, specifically a city.

candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: flightDistance
candidates.comment: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".

candidates.label: tripOrigin
candidates.comment: A trip origin relation between a trip and its starting location, prior to any destinations. Also called starting point, departure location, point of origin. Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: arrivalStation
candidates.comment: A station where a train trip concludes. Also called: train destination, end station, terminal station. Examples: "TrainTrip 456 arrivalStation 'Grand Central Station'", "TrainTrip from Rome arrivalStation 'Termini Station'", "TrainTrip to Berlin arrivalStation 'Hauptbahnhof'". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which specifies the specific platform within a station.

candidates.label: trainName
candidates.comment: A train name relation between a train trip and the specific name of the train. Also called name of train, railway name, train service name. Examples: "TrainTrip trainName 'The Orient Express'", "TrainTrip trainName 'Shinkansen Nozomi'", "TrainTrip trainName 'Eurostar'".

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

chosen_property.label: isHealthMinisterOf
chosen_property.definition: To be the health minister of a particular country.

candidates.label: healthCondition
candidates.comment: A health condition relation between a medical study, patient, or people audience and an associated medical condition. Also called medical diagnosis, health status, condition of. Examples: "A patient has a health condition of diabetes.", "A medical study focuses on a health condition.", "The target audience has a health condition of hypertension."

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: medicineSystem
candidates.comment: A medicine system relation between a medical entity and the system of medicine it belongs to. Also called: healthcare system, medical tradition, therapeutic approach. Examples: "Acupuncture medicineSystem 'Traditional Chinese Medicine'", "Homeopathic Remedy medicineSystem 'Homeopathic Medicine'", "Evidence-Based Treatment medicineSystem 'Evidence-Based Medicine'".

candidates.label: hospitalAffiliation
candidates.comment: A hospital affiliation relation between a physician and a hospital they are affiliated with. Also called affiliated hospital, associated hospital, hospital connection. Examples: "A physician has a hospital affiliation with 'General Hospital'.", "The doctor's hospital affiliation is a major medical center.", "This physician is affiliated with a specific hospital."

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: healthPlanDrugTier
candidates.comment: A drug tier relation between a health insurance plan or formulary and the tier classification of drugs it covers. Also called drug level, medication tier, formulary tier. Examples: "A health insurance plan has a drug tier for specialty drugs.", "The formulary includes a drug tier for preferred generics.", "This plan specifies drug tiers."

candidates.label: hasHealthAspect
candidates.comment: A health aspect relation between health topic content and the specific health aspect it addresses. Also called content aspect, topic aspect, health focus. Examples: "Health topic content has a health aspect of 'treatment'.", "The article has a health aspect of 'self-care'.", "This content addresses a health aspect of 'overview'."

candidates.label: healthPlanCoinsuranceRate
candidates.comment: A coinsurance rate relation between a health plan cost-sharing specification and the numerical rate of coinsurance. Also called coinsurance percentage, rate of coinsurance, coinsurance ratio. Examples: "Health plan cost-sharing has a coinsurance rate of 0.2.", "The specification includes a coinsurance rate of 0.15.", "This plan's coinsurance rate is 0.3."

candidates.label: usNPI
candidates.comment: A US NPI relation between a physician and their unique 10-digit National Provider Identifier issued in the United States. Also called NPI number, National Provider Identifier, US healthcare ID. Examples: "Physician usNPI '1234567890'", "Doctor usNPI '9876543210'", "Healthcare provider usNPI '1112223334'".

candidates.label: healthPlanNetworkId
candidates.comment: A health plan network identifier relation between a health plan network or medical organization and its unique network ID or name. Also called network ID, insurance network ID, network name. Examples: "A health plan network has a health plan network ID 'PPO-123'.", "The medical organization is part of a network with a specific health plan network ID.", "This network is identified by its health plan network ID."

chosen_property.label: setUpLabIn
chosen_property.definition: To have established a laboratory in a particular vehicle.

candidates.label: procedure
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the procedure for setting up, using, or installing a medical device. Also called usage instructions, installation guide, operational steps. Examples: A medical device has a procedure for 'surgical implantation'. The equipment includes a procedure for 'daily calibration'. The device's procedure outlines 'user operation steps'.

candidates.label: availableTest
candidates.comment: A diagnostic test or procedure offered by a diagnostic lab. Also called: lab test, diagnostic offering, test procedure. Examples: "DiagnosticLab 'LabCorp' availableTest 'Blood Test'", "DiagnosticLab 'Imaging Center' availableTest 'MRI Scan'."

candidates.label: subTest
candidates.comment: A component relation between a medical test panel and an individual medical test that is part of the panel. Also called "panel component", "included test", "part of test panel". Examples: "The blood panel has subTest a cholesterol test", "The medical test panel's subTest is a glucose measurement", "This panel includes several subTest procedures."

candidates.label: identifyingTest
candidates.comment: An identifying test relation between a medical sign and a medical test that can detect it. Also called diagnostic test, detection test, test for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying test of a blood panel.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying test.", "This sign requires an identifying test.". Distinct from identifyingExam, which refers to a physical examination.

candidates.label: preOp
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing the workup, testing, and preparations required before implanting a medical device. Also called pre-surgery instructions, pre-operative care, preparation protocol. Examples: A medical device has pre-op instructions for 'patient fasting'. The implant requires pre-op testing for 'compatibility'. The procedure involves pre-op preparations for 'sterilization'.

candidates.label: preparation
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing the typical preparation a patient must undergo before a medical procedure. Also called patient readiness, pre-procedure instructions, pre-op preparation. Examples: A medical procedure requires preparation like 'fasting for 8 hours'. The surgery involves preparation such as 'blood tests'. The diagnostic test needs preparation including 'avoiding certain medications'.

candidates.label: countryOfLastProcessing
candidates.comment: A final processing location relation between a product and the country where it underwent its last processing and testing before importation. Also called: last processed in, final testing country, pre-importation processing location. Examples: "Electronic Component" country of last processing "Malaysia", "Textile Product" country of last processing "Bangladesh", "Automotive Part" country of last processing "Thailand". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is about the origin of the product itself.

candidates.label: tissueSample
candidates.comment: A tissue sample relation between a pathology test and the type of tissue required for it. Also called sample type, biopsy type, specimen type. Examples: "Biopsy test tissueSample 'liver tissue'", "Pathology test tissueSample 'lymph node'", "Diagnostic test tissueSample 'skin biopsy'".

candidates.label: expressedIn
candidates.comment: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

chosen_property.label: provider
chosen_property.justification: Best fit among existing schema.org properties.

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: businessDays
candidates.comment: A specification of the days of the week when a service period or shipping delivery time typically operates. Also called "operating days", "days of operation", "working days". Examples: "Customer service businessDays Monday to Friday", "Standard shipping businessDays Weekday".

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: serviceOperator
candidates.comment: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.

candidates.label: isStoreOn
candidates.comment: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. Examples: An online store isStoreOn 'Amazon'. A small business's online store isStoreOn 'Etsy'. A vendor's shop isStoreOn 'eBay'.

candidates.label: hoursAvailable
candidates.comment: An hours available relation between a contact point, location feature specification, or service and its specified opening or availability hours. Also called operating hours, availability times, service hours. Examples: "A service has hours available from 9 AM to 5 PM.", "The contact point has hours available on weekdays.", "Location features specify hours available."

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: providesService
candidates.comment: A service provision relation between a service channel and the specific service it delivers. Also called channel delivers, service offered via, offers service. Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."

candidates.label: serverStatus
candidates.comment: The current operational status of a game server. Also called server state, game server condition, operational status. Examples: `Game Server A` serverStatus `Online`, `Game Server B` serverStatus `Offline`, `Game Server C` serverStatus `Maintenance`.
